sa: ओं ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति ।
किंकारणं ब्रह्म कुतः स्म जाता जीवामः केन क्व च संप्रतिष्ठाः  ।
अधिष्ठिताः केन सुखेतरेषु वर्तामहे ब्रह्मविदो व्यवस्थाम् ॥
iast: oṃ brahmavādino vadanti ।
kiṃkāraṇaṃ brahma kutaḥ sma jātā jīvāmaḥ kena kva ca saṃpratiṣṭhāḥ  ।
adhiṣṭhitāḥ kena sukhetareṣu vartāmahe brahmavido vyavasthām ॥
words: where? in what place? whither?(sometimes connected with particles ﾮMDBOﾯ~ṝha)

tr.text: Students of Brahman (i.e. the Vedas) discuss (among themselves): What is the cause ? (Is it) Brahman ? Whence are we born ? Why do we live ? Where is our final rest ? Under whose orders are we, who know the Brahman, subjected to the law of happiness and misery ?

sa: कालः स्वभावो नियतिर् यदृच्छा भूतानि योनिः पुरुषेति चिन्त्यम्  ।
संयोग एषां न त्व् आत्मभावाद् आत्मा ह्य् अनीशः सुखदुःखहेतोः ॥
iast: kālaḥ svabhāvo niyatir yadṛcchā bhūtāni yoniḥ puruṣeti cintyam  ।
saṃyoga eṣāṃ na tv ātmabhāvād ātmā hy anīśaḥ sukhaduḥkhahetoḥ ॥
words: one who has not a lord or superior

tr.text: Time, nature, law, chance, matter, energy, intelligence – neither these, nor combination of these, can bear examination because of their own birth, identity and the existence of the self. The self also is not a free agent, being under the sway of happiness and misery.

sa: ते ध्यानयोगानुगता अपश्यन् देवात्मशक्तिं स्वगुणैर् निगूढाम्  ।
यः कारणानि निखिलानि तानि कालात्मयुक्तान्य् अधितिष्ठत्य् एकः ॥
iast: te dhyānayogānugatā apaśyan devātmaśaktiṃ svaguṇair nigūḍhām  ।
yaḥ kāraṇāni nikhilāni tāni kālātmayuktāny adhitiṣṭhaty ekaḥ ॥
words: a single thread or strand of a cord or twine
to yoke or join or fasten or harness (horses or a chariot)

tr.text: Practising the method of meditation, they realized that Being who is the God of religion, the Self of philosophy and the Energy of science; who exists as the self-luminous power in everyone; who is the source of the intellect, emotions and will; who is one without a second; who presides over all the causes enumerated above, beginning with time and ending with the individual soul; and who had been incomprehensible because of the limitations of their own intellect.

sa: तम् एकनेमिं त्रिवृतं षोडशान्तं शतार्धारं विंशतिप्रत्यराभिः  ।
अष्टकैः षड्भिर् विश्वरूपैकपाशं त्रिमार्गभेदं द्विनिमित्तैकमोहम् ॥
iast: tam ekanemiṃ trivṛtaṃ ṣoḍaśāntaṃ śatārdhāraṃ viṃśatipratyarābhiḥ  ।
aṣṭakaiḥ ṣaḍbhir viśvarūpaikapāśaṃ trimārgabhedaṃ dvinimittaikamoham ॥
words: an intermediate spoke of a wheel
a whole consisting of eight parts

tr.text: We think of Him as the universe resembling a wheel which has one felly with a triple tyre, sixteen extremities, fifty spokes, twenty counter-spokes and six sets of eight; which is driven along three different roads by means of a belt that is single yet manifold; and which each revolution gives rise to two.

sa: पञ्चस्रोतोऽम्बुं पञ्चयोन्युग्रवक्त्रां पञ्चप्राणोर्मिं पञ्चबुद्ध्यादिमूलां  ।
पञ्चावर्तां पञ्चदुःखौघवेगां पञ्चाशद्भेदां पञ्चपर्वाम् अधीमः ॥
iast: pañcasroto’mbuṃ pañcayonyugravaktrāṃ pañcaprāṇormiṃ pañcabuddhyādimūlāṃ  ।
pañcāvartāṃ pañcaduḥkhaughavegāṃ pañcāśadbhedāṃ pañcaparvām adhīmaḥ ॥
words: the current or bed of a river; a river; stream
water; a kind of Andropogon; name of a metre (consisting of ninety syllables)
a wave; billow; (figuratively) wave of pain or passion or grief
flood; stream; rapid flow of water

tr.text: We think of Him (in His manifestation as the universe) who is like a river that contains the waters of five streams; that has five big turnings due to five causes; that has the five Pranas for the waves, the mind – the basis of five-fold perception – for the source, and the five-fold misery for its rapids; and that has five whirlpools, five branches and innumerable aspects.

sa: सर्वाजीवे सर्वसंस्थे बृहन्ते तस्मिन् हंसो भ्राम्यते ब्रह्मचक्रे  ।
पृथग् आत्मानं प्रेरितारं च मत्वा जुष्टस् ततस् तेनामृतत्वम् एति ॥
iast: sarvājīve sarvasaṃsthe bṛhante tasmin haṃso bhrāmyate brahmacakre  ।
pṛthag ātmānaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā juṣṭas tatas tenāmṛtatvam eti ॥
words: standing together; standing or staying or resting or being in or on; contained in
to confuse; to move or roam about; to cause to wander
one who urges or incites; an inciter

tr.text: In this infinite wheel of Brahman, in which everything lives and rests, the pilgrim soul is whirled about. Knowing the individual soul, hitherto regarded as separate, to be itself the Moving Force, and blessed by Him, it attains immortality.

sa: उद्गीतम् एतत् परमं तु ब्रह्म तस्मिंस् त्रयं स्वप्रतिष्ठाक्षरं च  ।
अत्रान्तरं ब्रह्मविदो विदित्वा लीना ब्रह्मणि तत्परा योनिमुक्ताः ॥
iast: udgītam etat paramaṃ tu brahma tasmiṃs trayaṃ svapratiṣṭhākṣaraṃ ca  ।
atrāntaraṃ brahmavido viditvā līnā brahmaṇi tatparā yonimuktāḥ ॥
words: to cling or press closely; to stick or adhere to; to remain sticking
following that or thereupon; having that as one's highest object or aim

tr.text: This is expressly declared to be the Supreme Brahman. In that is the triad. It is the firm support, and it is the imperishable. Knowing the inner essence of this, the knowers of Veda become devoted to Brahman, merge themselves in It, and are released from birth.

sa: संयुक्तम् एतत् क्षरम् अक्षरं च व्यक्ताव्यक्तं भरते विश्वम् ईशः  ।
अनीशश् चात्मा बध्यते भोक्तृभावाज् ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपाशैः ॥
iast: saṃyuktam etat kṣaram akṣaraṃ ca vyaktāvyaktaṃ bharate viśvam īśaḥ  ।
anīśaś cātmā badhyate bhoktṛbhāvāj jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ ॥
words: to bind; to tie; to fix

tr.text: The Lord supports this universe, which consists of a combination of the perishable and the imperishable, the manifest and the unmanifest. As long as the self does not know the Lord, it gets attached to worldly pleasures, and is bound; but when it knows Him, all fetters fall away from it.

sa: ज्ञाज्ञौ द्वाव् अजाव् ईशनीशाव् अजा ह्य् एका भोक्तृभोगार्थयुक्ता  ।
अनन्तश् चात्मा विश्वरूपो ह्य् अकर्ता त्रयं यदा विन्दते ब्रह्मम् एतत् ॥
iast: jñājñau dvāv ajāv īśanīśāv ajā hy ekā bhoktṛbhogārthayuktā  ।
anantaś cātmā viśvarūpo hy akartā trayaṃ yadā vindate brahmam etat ॥

tr.text: The conscious subject and the unconscious object, the master and the dependent, are both unborn. She, too, who is engaged in bringing about the relation of the enjoyer and the enjoyed (or between these two), is unborn. When all these three are realized as Brahman, the self becomes infinite, universal and free from the sense of agentship.

sa: क्षरं प्रधानम् अमृताक्षरं हरः क्षरात्मानाव् ईशते देव एकः  ।
तस्याभिध्यानाद् योजनात् तत्त्वभावाद् भूयश् चान्ते विश्वमायानिवृत्तिः ॥
iast: kṣaraṃ pradhānam amṛtākṣaraṃ haraḥ kṣarātmānāv īśate deva ekaḥ  ।
tasyābhidhyānād yojanāt tattvabhāvād bhūyaś cānte viśvamāyānivṛttiḥ ॥
words: a chief thing or person; the principal or first; primary matter or nature
name of Śiva; name of a Dānava; name of a monkey

tr.text: Matter is perishable, but God is imperishable and immortal. He, the only God, rules over the perishable matter and individual souls. By meditating on him, by uniting with Him, and by becoming one with Him, there is cessation of all illusion in the end.

sa: ज्ञात्वा देवं सर्वपाशापहानिः क्षीनैः क्लेशैर् जन्ममृत्युप्रहाणिः  ।
तस्याभिध्यानात् तृतीयं देहभेदे विश्वैश्वर्यं केवल आप्तकामः ॥
iast: jñātvā devaṃ sarvapāśāpahāniḥ kṣīnaiḥ kleśair janmamṛtyuprahāṇiḥ  ।
tasyābhidhyānāt tṛtīyaṃ dehabhede viśvaiśvaryaṃ kevala āptakāmaḥ ॥
words: the state of being a mighty lord; sovereignty; supremacy

tr.text: With the knowledge of God, all fetters fall off. With the waning of ignorance, birth and death cease. Going beyond the consciousness of the body by meditating on Him, one reaches the third state, viz., the universal lordship. All his desires are satisfied, and he becomes one without a second.

sa: एतज् ज्ञेयं नित्यम् एवात्मसंस्थं नातः परं वेदितव्यं हि किंचित्  ।
भोक्ता भोग्यं प्रेरितारं च मत्वा सर्वं प्रोक्तं त्रिविधं ब्रह्मम् एतत् ॥
iast: etaj jñeyaṃ nityam evātmasaṃsthaṃ nātaḥ paraṃ veditavyaṃ hi kiṃcit  ।
bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā sarvaṃ proktaṃ trividhaṃ brahmam etat ॥
words: standing together; standing or staying or resting or being in or on; contained in
an object of enjoyment; possession; money
one who urges or incites; an inciter

tr.text: This is to be known as eternally existing in one’s own self. Indeed, there is nothing to be known beyond this. As a result of meditation the enjoyer, the enjoyed and the power which brings about the enjoyment – all are declared to be the three aspects of Brahman.

sa: वह्नेर् यथा योनिगतस्य मूर्तिर् न दृश्यते नैव च लिङ्गनाशः  ।
स भूय एवेन्धनयोनिगृह्यस् तद्वोभयं वै प्रणवेन देहे ॥
iast: vahner yathā yonigatasya mūrtir na dṛśyate naiva ca liṅganāśaḥ  ।
sa bhūya evendhanayonigṛhyas tadvobhayaṃ vai praṇavena dehe ॥
words: any animal that draws or bears along; a draught animal; horse

tr.text: Fire is not perceived in its source, the fire-stick, till it is ignited by percussion. The subtle essence of fire, nevertheless, is not absent in the stick; for fire can be obtained from the source, the fire-stick, by striking again. (The state of the Atman before and after realization). By meditating on the Pranava, the Atman is perceived manifestly in the body, (but it was there in a latent state even before realization).

sa: स्वदेहम् अरणिं कृत्वा प्रणवं चोत्तरारणिं  ।
ध्याननिर्मथनाभ्यासाद् देवं पश्येन् निगूढवत् ॥
iast: svadeham araṇiṃ kṛtvā praṇavaṃ cottarāraṇiṃ  ।
dhyānanirmathanābhyāsād devaṃ paśyen nigūḍhavat ॥
words: the upper araṇi which is also called Pramantha or churner
the act of adding anything; (in Gr.) "what is prefixed"

tr.text: Making one’s own body the lower piece of wood, and the Pranava the upper piece of wood, and practising churning in the form of meditation, one should realize God as one would find out something hidden.

sa: तिलेषु तैलं दधनीव सर्पिर् आपः स्रोतःस्व् अरणीषु चाग्निः  ।
एवम् आत्मा आत्मनि गृह्यते ऽसौ सत्येनैनं तपसा यो ऽनुपश्यति ॥
iast: tileṣu tailaṃ dadhanīva sarpir āpaḥ srotaḥsv araṇīṣu cāgniḥ  ।
evam ātmā ātmani gṛhyate ’sau satyenainaṃ tapasā yo ’nupaśyati ॥
words: the current or bed of a river; a river; stream

tr.text: As oil in sesame seeds, as butter in curds, as water in underground springs, as fire in wood, even so this Self is perceived in the self. He who, by means of truthfulness, self-control and concentration, looks again and again for this Self, which is all-pervading like butter contained in milk, and which is rooted in self-knowledge and meditation – he becomes that Supreme Brahman, the destroyer of ignorance.

sa: सर्वव्यापिनम् आत्मानं क्षीरे सर्पिर् इवार्पितम्  ।
आत्मविद्यातपोमूलं तद् ब्रह्मोपनिषत्परं तद् ब्रह्मोपनिषत्परम् ॥
iast: sarvavyāpinam ātmānaṃ kṣīre sarpir ivārpitam  ।
ātmavidyātapomūlaṃ tad brahmopaniṣatparaṃ tad brahmopaniṣatparam ॥
words: milk; thickened milk; the milky juice or sap of plants

tr.text: As oil in sesame seeds, as butter in curds, as water in underground springs, as fire in wood, even so this Self is perceived in the self. He who, by means of truthfulness, self-control and concentration, looks again and again for this Self, which is all-pervading like butter contained in milk, and which is rooted in self-knowledge and meditation – he becomes that Supreme Brahman, the destroyer of ignorance.
